name: @onhand-mcp/cli
stderr:
onhand 0.1.0

Usage:
  onhand find      Find a business by name
  onhand search    Search items and services near a point
  onhand business  Show one business profile
  onhand ask       Ask a business's approved answers a question
  onhand slots     List the next open appointment slots
  onhand reviews   List receipt-backed reviews

Your business (needs a sign-in):
  onhand company           Show your business's profile
  onhand locations         List your business's locations and their ids
  onhand connections       List your connected point-of-sale and booking sources
  onhand subscription      Show what your organization pays for
  onhand org list          List your organizations
  onhand org use "<name>"  Choose the organization you act for
  onhand link connection   Page where you connect or change a source
  onhand link billing      Page where you manage billing
  onhand hours set         Change one location's opening hours
  onhand profile set       Change your business's name, phone or categories

Account and tools:
  onhand login [--no-browser]
  onhand whoami [--json]
  onhand logout
  onhand tools [--json]
  onhand tool <name> [--input '<json object>'] [--json]

Run "onhand <command> --help" for a command's flags.

Options:
  --json           Print one JSON document on stdout instead of a table
  --no-color       Accepted; this version prints no colour
  --base-url <url> Server origin (default https://mcp.askonhand.com, env ONHAND_BASE_URL);
                   https, or http to localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]
  --input <json>   Tool arguments as a JSON object (default {})
  --no-browser     login: print the address instead of opening a browser,
                   then paste back the address the browser ended on
  --provider, --action  link connection: which source and what to do
  --role <role>    org use: pick between organizations that share a name
  --dry-run        hours set, profile set: show the change and apply nothing
  --yes            hours set, profile set: apply without asking
  -h, --help       Show this help
  --version        Show the version

Sign-in (login) opens your browser and saves the sign-in for that server in the
system keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret
Service). When there is none, or it is locked, the sign-in goes in
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/onhand/credentials.json (default ~/.config/onhand/), readable
only by you on macOS and Linux (Windows relies on your profile's permissions).
ONHAND_CREDENTIAL_STORE=file skips the keychain. whoami shows who you are signed in as and your organizations;
logout removes the saved sign-in. ONHAND_ACCESS_TOKEN, if set, is used as the
access token and never stored. ONHAND_ISSUER, ONHAND_CLIENT_ID and
ONHAND_RESOURCE choose where to sign in.
Tables cut long values; use --json for the full text.

Exit codes:
  0  Success
  1  Unexpected error
  2  Bad usage or input failed validation
  3  Not signed in, or the access token was not accepted
  4  Not allowed (insufficient_scope, agent_request_refused, or your organization role: forbidden)
  5  Action needed in the browser or a choice (link_required, setup_required, verification_pending, selection_required)
  6  Not found
  7  Rate limited or service unavailable after retries
  8  Declined or timed out
onhand: Unknown command or wrong number of arguments.
